articles.title: NFL Rules on CJGJ's Appeal of 1-Game Suspension for Spitting at Brock Bowers, Raiders
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson will have to serve his punishment for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum on Sunday.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson will have to serve his punishment for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum on Sunday.

The NFL announced on Thursday that Jordy Nelson, who was jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFLPA as the hearing officer for Gardner-Johnson's appeal, has upheld his one-game suspension for the incident.

The Bills (5-1) are on a bye this week, so Gardner-Johnson will miss their Week 8 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens on Nov. 1.

NFL player suspended for spitting on opponent

Per ESPN's Nick Suss , the league said in a statement earlier this week that Gardner-Johnson violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship." Cameras caught him spitting in the direction of Bowers and Linderbaum shortly before halftime, and he was ejected from the game.

After the Bills' 33-30 win, Gardner-Johnson told reporters that he apologized to his teammates in the locker room, and he admitted that his actions weren't sparked by a specific incident.

"We were just arguing and talking," he said. "It was nothing negative. He ain't do nothing to me. It was just in the heat of the game, arguing and talking s--t. That gesture isn't warranted."

Gardner-Johnson also posted an apology on social media, writing, "My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed. The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game."

As an eight-year veteran, Gardner-Johnson is one of the leaders of a Buffalo team looking to make it to the Super Bowl, so he should try to avoid any further infractions that would keep him off the field.

articles.title: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update, Latest Rumors on RB's Status for Cardinals vs. Broncos
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.
articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love is expected to miss Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz .

An ankle injury sidelined the first-round pick for Arizona's 18-16 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Week 6.

Bam Knight ran for 80 yards on 15 carries against L.A., and Tyler Allgeier chipped in with 38 yards on the ground.

The Broncos have been one of the NFL's worst teams against the run. They're 31st in yards allowed at 139.8 per game, and they're giving up 4.7 yards per carry.

The matchup would seemingly present a great opportunity for Love to get his rookie campaign on track after an inconsistent start. He has run for 245 yards and one touchdown while averaging 3.7 yards per carry in five appearances.

That's not the kind of return you want to see from a running back selected third overall.

Rather than taking advantage of Denver's porous defense, Love will have to wait another week to reestablish himself in Arizona's backfield.

Knight and Allgeier, meanwhile, have one more game to deliver the kind of performance that could force coach Mike LaFleur to rethink the hierarchy in the running game once Love is back healthy.

articles.title: Los Angeles Rams are spiralling, Sean McVay looks lost and Aaron Donald is being let down
articles.summary: Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds and Phoebe Schecter discuss the 'spiralling' Los Angeles Rams as Sean McVay's supposed 'super-team' seek to recover after a dismal start to the season; watch the Rams face the Las Vegas Raiders at 8.25pm live on Sky Sports this Sunday
articles.body:
Sean McVay's injury-stricken side enter 2-4 and bottom of the NFC West having so far fallen desperately short of soaring expectations for a team billed as Super Bowl favourites coming into the year.

Myles Garrett remains sidelined, Matthew Stafford just lost a red-hot Davante Adams to injury and their league-worst special teams unit remain a debilitating hindrance.

Three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald didn't come back for this.

"I feel a bit tight on Aaron Donald because he ultimately came out of retirement to play with Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, Ponna Ford, and none of them are playing. It's just Aaron Donald," said Schecter on Inside the Huddle .

"It feels like they need to find a way to salvage their season. But I just think it's so much more than just stats," Schecter added.

"When you're looking at this team and you're looking at the injuries that they have, losing Davante Adams, nobody wants to see that. He is your red zone guy, he is someone who gives so much confidence, you just throw it up down there and he'll find a way.

"You're starting to slowly chip away at all these receivers. I've never seen Sean McVay just look so lost or, you know, almost like hurt by the whole situation.

"It's a huge challenge for the Rams. I don't know how they find a way to salvage themselves."

McVay's Rams are still averaging the third most yards on offense in the NFL while ranking in passing yards, but sit down in 15th in rushing. Reigning MVP Matthew Stafford meanwhile tops the league in passing yards with 1,794 through six weeks, and has thrown 11 touchdowns to six interceptions, albeit while being 15th in EPA/play (an advanced metric measuring down-to-down efficiency).

Having been missing Puka Nacua earlier in the season, they are now without Adams having entered with hopes of the pair featuring prominently alongside one another. Injuries at the tight end position have meanwhile hindered McVay's multiple tight end sets, which proved so successful last season .

"You look at who this Rams team is, they're starting to be quite predictable," said Schecter. "They've called a pass play on 65 percent of offensive plays, that's really quite skewed, and you need to have that run game going.

"I think that's part of it, too.You're starting to see the athletes from within, Kyren Williams coming out being like, I don't know why I'm not running the ball. I don't know why I'm not playing as much. And that's never what you want.

"We talk about it so much with other teams, like the Eagles, for example.And it becomes a really big deal. The Rams are in trouble right now. And if they're supposed to be this Super Bowl team, they've got to find a way to pull together soon."

The Rams are coming off an 18-16 upset defeat to the Arizona Cardinals, having fallen to the Buffalo Bills in overtime the previous week. Their special-teams woes have reared their ugly head once again, with Harrison Mevis released following his role in the loss to Buffalo, only for his replacement, Blake Grupe, to suffer a season-ending ACL injury while attempting to make a tackle on a return against Arizona last weekend.

Awaiting them is a Raiders team sitting 3-3 and seemingly exceeding early expectations behind Kirk Cousins during Klint Kubiak's first season as head coach.

"It feels it feels like it's spiralling down the drainpipe at the moment," said Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds.

"McVay is somebody to monitor because he's very frustrated, probably frustrated that when he didn't have Puka Nacua, he had Davante Adams. Now he's got Nacua back and out goes Adams.

"They're beating themselves. I think some of Sean McVay's play, he seems to regret after every game, he seems to regret something he did.

"Now here comes Kirk Cousins, who's playing very well for the Raiders. And it's in Las Vegas.This is a big challenge for the Rams."

articles.title: Week 7 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em, Play or Bench Advice on Top Fantasy Football NFL Stars
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL season has been an unpredictable one, to say the least. The uncertainty has extended to fantasy football, where several expected stars have disappointed, and several surprises have risen through the ranks.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season has been an unpredictable one, to say the least. The uncertainty has extended to fantasy football, where several expected stars have disappointed, and several surprises have risen through the ranks.

Of course, mainstays like Joe Burrow, Justin Jefferson, Jahmyr Gibbs, and Brock Bowers will remain glued to starting lineups for as long as they're healthy.

It's those second-tier stars that have been harder to figure out this season, and neither injuries nor bye weeks have helped. This week, the Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers, and Washington Commanders will be out of action.

Here, you'll find some start/sit recommendations for Week 7's fringe stars, based on recent production, projected roles, individual matchups, and point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Kyler Murray hasn't been great thus far, but the Minnesota Vikings have a tremendous skill group and are coming out of their bye week. Hopefully, Kevin O'Connell spent the week dialing up ways to get Murray into more of a rhythm.

The Vikings will also host an Indianapolis Colts team that has struggled defensively. The Colts have surrendered the 11th-most fantasy points to opposing QBs and are unlikely to have cornerback Sauce Gardner because of a calf injury.

Sam Darnold had arguably his worst game since joining the Seattle Seahawks in last week's loss to the Denver Broncos. He's becoming a legitimate drop candidate, and he certainly can't be trusted this week against the visiting Kansas City Chiefs.

If Darnold doesn't trust what he's seeing from opposing defenses, he's going to have a tough time against Steve Spagnuolo's unit. The Chiefs have surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Start: Bucky Irving, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving was largely held in check by the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 6. Despite seeing a high-volume workload, he was held to 46 rushing yards, two catches, and 6.9 fantasy points.

Managers should trust Irving to rebound in Week 7, though. He'll maintain a heavy workload and faces a much better matchup against the rival Carolina Panthers. Carolina has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing RBs this season.

New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh essentially punished Cam Skattebo for his fumbles by leaving him out of the offensive game plan in Week 6. The former starter didn't see a single touch during the loss to the New Orleans Saints.

While Skattebo may be back in the rotation this week, managers should trust a return to form. The Giants will visit the Houston Texans, who have surrendered the 11th-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs this season.

As a rotational player, Skattebo can be sat, along with:

Neither the Detroit Lions nor the Green Bay Packers have been great defensively this season. We're likely to see offensive fireworks when the two NFC North rivals face off this weekend, which makes stars like Amon-Ra St. Brown and Christian Watson obvious must-starts.

Detroit's No. 2 receiver, Jameson Williams, should get in on the action early and often. He's topped 16 fantasy points in each of his last two games and should have another double-digit outing as St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs draw Green Bay's defensive focus.

Colts receiver Josh Downs hasn't benefited from Alec Pierce's injury as much as fantasy managers might have expected. While he did reach double-digit fantasy points in Weeks 2 and 3, he hasn't reached nine points since.

Indy's passing attack simply hasn't been very good this season, and it'll face a tough Vikings defense in Week 7. Minnesota has surrendered the fourth-fewest fantasy points to opposing WRs this season.

Start: Dallas Goedert, Philadelphia Eagles

With Jalen Hurts out for the year due to blood clots, the Philadelphia Eagles will rely on Tanner McKee for the foreseeable future. Philly's offense didn't look great with McKee behind center in Week 6, but he did manage to find his playmakers.

Tight end Dallas Goedert caught six passes for 61 yards on Sunday, and he should have another big outing against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night. Dallas has merely average against opposing tight ends and pretty much rotten overall defensively.

The Eagles have also been pretty average against opposing tight ends and have surrendered an average of 9.3 fantasy points to the position. However, Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson has slipped out of Dallas' game plan due to the emergence of third receiver Ryan Flournoy.

Ferguson has just one double-digit fantasy outing this season and has failed to reach five fantasy points for three consecutive games. It's impossible to trust him on the road in Philadelphia.

articles.title: Jordan Elliott: Defensive tackle released by Tenessee Titans after pulling gun in car park
articles.summary: Defensive tackle Jordan Elliott is released by the Tennessee Titans after he pulled a gun in the car park of the team facility.
articles.body:
Defensive tackle Jordan Elliott has been released by the Tennessee Titans after he pulled a gun in the car park of the team facility.

Titans coach Robert Saleh confirmed on Tuesday reports that Elliott retrieved a gun from his car after an altercation with JC Latham during practice on 15 October.

The 28-year-old did not play in Sunday's victory against the Indianapolis Colts and was released by the Titans on Tuesday over what the club called an "incident".

"Just pause with regards to the news that Jordan had a gun," Saleh said.

"This is a man who is a father, a great husband. This is a man who has never committed a crime in his entire life.

"And he pulled a gun in the parking lot. Why did he go off the rails and grab a gun? To me, those are small signs of a cry for help. Obviously there is something greater happening."

Offensive tackle Latham called the altercation with Elliott an "unfortunate situation" that happened "just in the heat of the moment".

"Never been no bad blood between us two. We never actually had an argument leading up to it," Latham said.

"I do think mental health is extremely important and that's just one of those situations where you pray for a guy like that and, if you can, reach out to him, hope for the best for him. It's nothing personal on my end."

Elliott, who previously played for San Francisco and Cleveland, has appeared in five games this season.

Saleh said he would still recommend Elliott to another franchise.

"My message to 31 other teams would be if you need a hell of a run-stopping D-tackle that can help you on a play-off run, give me a call, I'll tell you everything you need to know about him," he said.

"I will stand on the table for Jordan's character. Unfortunately rules are rules with regards to guns on property, and sometimes it's far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they're down."

articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Bears vs. Patriots features two hot teams with exciting young QBs
articles.summary: Drake Maye and Caleb Williams both look like future NFL stars.
articles.body:
The 2024 NFL Draft made history. It was the first time six quarterbacks were taken in the top 12 picks.

There's plenty of time to watch all six quarterbacks' careers play out and figure out how they rank. But early in their third seasons, two quarterbacks from that class seem to be separating themselves: Caleb Williams of the Chicago Bears and Drake Maye of the New England Patriots (Jayden Daniels of the Washington Commanders could make it a three-way conversation, but he needs to stay healthy).

On Thursday night, Maye and Williams get the national stage as the Bears and Patriots face off. The teams around those quarterbacks are pretty good too.

The Patriots have shaken off a slow start to win three in a row, a streak that included an impressive win at the Buffalo Bills. Maye's struggles to begin the season, a slump that extended back to last postseason, are over too. Over the last three games he has 10 passing touchdowns and one interception. Maye came one vote from winning NFL MVP last season and over the last three games he has looked like that player who was a breakout star last season.

The Patriots and Bears are both 4-2, arriving at that record in different ways. The Patriots started slow and have heated up. The Bears came firing out of the gate by posting 59 points against the Carolina Panthers in the opener, but in Week 2 the offense struggled and Williams injured his hamstring. The Bears stayed afloat by winning two of three games with Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent at quarterback, though the third game in that stretch was a bad 31-7 road loss to the Packers. Williams returned last week and the Bears were up 31-7 at the Atlanta Falcons in the fourth quarter. Chicago let up and the Falcons got back in the game, but the Bears delivered a key defensive stop to win 31-23.

With Williams healthy and Maye on fire, Thursday night should be a fun showdown between a pair of 24-year-old quarterbacks who should be stars for many years to come. Both teams might be capable of deep playoff runs this season, as well.

Both teams are in similar situations. The Patriots are chasing the Bills in the AFC East and can't afford to let Buffalo distance itself in the race. The Bears are off to a good start too but are looking up at the 5-0 Vikings in the NFC North. The difference for the Bears is their entire division is in the race. Every team is above .500 and capable of winning the division. For that reason, we'll say the Bears have a little more on the line for Thursday night. But the stakes are high for each team, because one of them will be 5-2 and feeling very good about where their season is headed.

The Patriots traded a first-round draft pick for Brown to give them a true No. 1 receiver and transform their offense. That hasn't happened because Brown suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 and went on injured reserve. He came off IR for Week 6 and understandably was rusty, with just three catches for 27 yards. He had three drops.

That is uncharacteristic and seems unlikely to repeat. If the Patriots can get Brown to play to his normal level, it would improve an offense that is already on a hot streak. Brown becoming a factor in the offense is even more important with Romeo Doubs going on injured reserve with a shoulder injury . Two weeks ago the Bears were picked apart by Jordan Love and the Packers, who repeatedly beat the secondary deep. Brown being able to generate some explosive plays could be the difference in what should be a close game.

The Bears are 3-point home favorites against the suddenly red-hot Patriots on Thursday night. Chicago welcomed Caleb Williams back on Sunday against Atlanta, and the Bears' offense looked borderline unstoppable for stretches of the game in building a 31-7 lead, before two late Atlanta scores made the final closer than it should've been. Drake Maye has turned his season around, but will have his hands full trying to keep up with Chicago's offense. This total has already gone up a couple points from its opener, but I expect a great game between two potential playoff teams in this one that goes over the total of 50.5.

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Fantasy football storylines, by Scott Pianowski

Week 7 kicks off with a fun matchup between the Patriots and Bears, looking at a juicy 50.5 total. Here are three themes to track from a fantasy perspective.

1. What does the New England backfield look like? The Patriots used three primary backs in the win over the Jets on Sunday, and it was unheralded Corey Kiner who closed the game out. Rhamondre Stevenson is a borderline start here, and TreVeyon Henderson a bench stash (at best) for now.

2. Have the Bears unlocked their best pass catchers? Obviously getting QB Caleb Williams back last week was a huge lift, but it was also refreshing to see Colston Loveland and Luther Burden III reach expectations. Perhaps Loveland, Burden and Rome Odunze are finally ready to validate their aggressive summer ADPs.

3. Can A.J. Brown get back in form? Brown's first game back from his ankle injury was an unqualified mess — just 27 yards and a handful of drops. The Patriots want Brown to be their alpha, but Drake Maye has been productive of late spreading the ball around.

articles.title: Giants DC Calls Out 'Traitors' Who Don't Give Enough Effort on Defense After Loss to Saints
articles.summary: Whenever an NFL defensive coordinator drops the word "traitors" when talking about the effort level of his unit, it's going to draw attention.
articles.body:
Whenever an NFL defensive coordinator drops the word "traitors" when talking about the effort level of his unit, it's going to draw attention.

And that is exactly what happened Thursday with the New York Giants.

"I wasn't happy with our effort running to the ball," Giants DC Dennard Wilson told reporters when discussing the loss to the New Orleans Saints and describing those who don't run to the ball as "traitors."

He then said he plans to "confront everything" when asked how New York will deal with the situation.

"When you have behavior that's unacceptable, we're not gonna accept it," Wilson continued. "And if you don't change the behaviors, we have to change the players."

New York's defense struggled in the 34-27 loss to the Saints, giving up three touchdown passes to zero interceptions from Tyler Shough and allowing the visitors to run for 175 yards and a touchdown.

The Giants built a double-digit lead in the second quarter but found themselves behind by as many as 24 points before J.J. McCarthy closed the gap with an impressive late performance after he entered the game for Jameis Winston.

Following the loss, New York is 19th in the league in points allowed per game. That defense was also unable to protect a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter of the previous game against the Washington Commanders, which ended in a 27-27 tie.

With Wilson calling out the effort level in such a head-turning manner, the defense will be firmly under the spotlight Sunday when it faces the Houston Texans. Another poor performance could lead to personnel changes, especially since the DC said the plan is to "confront everything."

articles.title: Steelers cancel Paris fan event over fears of unrest while NFL pushes ahead with its own event and game
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers canceled their Paris fan event amid unrest, breaking from the NFL's stance that Sunday's game and its own event are safe.
articles.body: The NFL has insisted multiple times this week that Sunday's game in France will be safe to play and safe for fans to attend amid civil unrest in Paris, but the Pittsburgh Steelers showed a different side to that confidence on Thursday by canceling one of their fan events. The club confirmed to OutKick that it has canceled a Steelers House fan event scheduled for this week. "Following recent events in the Bastille neighborhood and after careful consideration, we felt it appropriate not to move forward with the planned Steelers House fan event in Paris," the club announced. This isn't the lone crack in the "all is well" armor the NFL has put on about this event. Earlier this week, Dani Watt, the wife of Steelers defensive end TJ Watt, questioned publicly why the game has not been moved. TJ WATT'S WIFE BREAKS RANKS WITH NFL MARCH TOWARD PARIS GAME QUESTIONING HOW PLAYING THERE MAKES SENSE NFL SAYS FIRST REGULAR-SEASON GAME IN FRANCE REMAINS ON TRACK DESPITE GROWING UNREST IN PARIS This is an obvious break from the the league's narrative that the civil unrest in Paris and other parts of France will not hinder it from playing its game and, indeed, holding a fan event of its own. The NFL on Thursday told OutKick that its own NFL Fan House event scheduled for Friday and Saturday remains as scheduled. "It's happening," a league spokesman said. So what we have is the NFL taking another bold step in virtually guaranteeing the safety of its players and fans during the game, but also doing the same for a fan event over a two-day span at 46 Rue Cambon in Paris. NEW ORLEANS SAINTS ARRIVE IN FRANCE WITH SAFETY TOP OF MIND AHEAD OF NFL'S FIRST PARIS GAME And this is where you should know it's not only the NFL that seems confident about the safety of Americans tied to the game in France. On Wednesday, NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said he's going to the game and he spoke with United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio about the event in recent days about moving forward with the game. Rubio told OutKick that the American embassy in France believes the game "will be fine." SECRETARY OF STATE MARCO RUBIO GIVES NFL COMMISSIONER ROGER GOODELL ASSURANCES NFL GAME IN FRANCE âWILL BE FINEâ So the NFL is moving ahead, including with its own fan event at which multiple thousand French and American football fans are expected in the days prior to the game. "There's nothing more important from our standpoint than the teams' security, the fans' security, everybody involved with this game," NFL executive vice president Peter O'Reilly said at the League Fall Meeting this week. "Again, we've made all the preparations," Goodell said. "We've been in touch with all the appropriate authorities." FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Tom Brady Makes Strong Statement on 49ers Ahead of Falcons Game
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers improved to 6-0 following their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders on Monday night. They’re now one of just three unbeaten team...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers improved to 6-0 following their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders on Monday night.

They're now one of just three unbeaten teams remaining, and NFL legend and Fox Sports announcer Tom Brady acknowledged their early-season success this week before heading to Atlanta on Sunday for a matchup aaginst the Falcons.

Every Wednesday, Brady releases his weekly NFL power rankings, listing the 10 teams he believes are the best in the league.

The rankings often shift from week to week, but the team at the top hasn't changed in weeks. Brady continues to rank the 49ers ahead of the two other undefeated teams, the Kansas City Chiefs and Minnesota Vikings.

"Yep. No surprise here. The Niners stay undefeated on Monday Night Football which means they stay number one in my power rankings," said Brady. "They head to Atlanta next week looking to cruise into a bye at a perfect 7-0. Something we didn't see coming as the injuries piled up. This team exemplifies the next man up mentality though which bodes well as the gauntlet of an NFL season rolls on."

49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is playing as well as anyone at his position in the league right now, and Brady, who knows plenty about succeeding as a QB, discussed what he's seen from the former seventh-round pick this season.

"He's playing like one of the MVP favorites right now… distributing the ball to Evans, to Kittle, McCaffrey, making plays on the move, extending plays on third down, scrambling when he needs to. He's making so many impact plays. So proud of him the way that he's playing," said Brady last week."The true field general out there getting his team in the right place. Way to go, Brock.

"I think as a quarterback you're always supposed to be managing every game. You're managing every situation, you're the coach on the field, you're the one that gets the last swipe at the pencil, you're the checks and balances of the whole offense and when it at times to make a play out there you do that too." You do what's easy and when it requires you do what's hard and sometimes you gotta make things happen with your legs and Brock's been able to do that."

articles.title: Nick Suzuki Injury Ends Iron Man Streak and Leaves Huge Hole for Montreal Canadiens
articles.summary: On Thursday morning, the Montreal Canadiens made an announcement that the NHL newswire has never seen before. Their captain is injured and will be out for tw...
articles.body:
On Thursday morning, the Montreal Canadiens made an announcement that the NHL newswire has never seen before. Their captain is injured and will be out for two to four weeks. The Nick Suzuki injury ends his iron man streak at 546 games, and creates a crater-size hole in the Montreal Canadiens lineup.

Nick Suzuki was the 13th overall pick of the Vegas Golden Knights in the 2017 NHL Entry Draft. Just over a year later, on September 10, 2018, Suzuki was traded to the Montreal Canadiens in a package to acquire Max Pacioretty . Following the trade, Suzuki played one more season in the Ontario Hockey League. He made the Montreal Canadiens team in the 2019-20 season without playing one game in the American Hockey League.

On October 12, 2021, the Montreal Canadiens signed Nick Suzuki to an eight-year, $63 million contract. This contract would become the cornerstone of team-friendly contracts signed by their core, allowing the Canadiens to maintain a solid cap structure and open options for adding contracts to strengthen their team. The latest was when Ivan Demidov extended this past summer.

Suzuki has played 546 regular season games for the Montreal Canadiens, and 56 Stanley Cup Playoff games. He has never missed one game due to injury until now, ending his iron man streak at 546 games.

Concerns Growing as Nick Suzuki Injury Leaves Hole a Centre

There is not one player on the Montreal Canadiens whose absence will be felt more than the absence of Nick Suzuki. Suzuki was named the Habs 31st captain before the start of the 2022-23 season, identifying him as the face of the newly rebuilt Canadiens. His leadership will be missed in the room, along with his production on the ice. Suzuki scored 101 points last season, and already has 12 points in nine games in this season.

His loss will also be felt because of an already thin centre group, and an ailing top six. Montreal was actively trying to add a top-six centre this past summer to support Suzuki, without success. Then top-six forward Ivan Demidov was lost to injury , thinning the top six further. Coach Martin St. Louis will be forced to be very creative in designing his lines in Suzuki's absence.

The Canadiens have also been rumoured to be interested in centreman Dylan Larkin , while also actively exploring other options. The Nick Suzuki injury may intensify their urgency to make a trade to strengthen their top six. Such a move will prove challenging since other teams will be more likely to offer an anchor than a life jacket in this situation.

Nick Suzuki Injury Opens Door for Owen Beck

Just yesterday, with Florian Xhekaj set to return to the lineup following a brief injury, Owen Beck was loaned back to the Laval Rocket. This morning, after announcing the Nick Suzuki injury, the Canadiens followed up with an announcement that they had recalled Owen Beck.

Beck is not an option to join the top six and provide any sort of relief. But he may be able to fill a fourth line role while one of the veterans climbs the depth chart to try and an hold things together while Suzuki is sidelined.

The Nick Suzuki injury came as an unwelcome surprise to fans of the Montreal Canadiens on Thursday. The Habs have not had to play without Suzuki since their rebuild began, and they are about to find out just how important he is to their success. This is an opportunity for other players on the roster to step up and help replace what he brings to the table. It is also a chance for management to show how creative they can be in the face of challenge, and add reinforcements to their group.

articles.title: JJ Watt gets multiyear deal as lead analyst for 'NFL on CBS'
articles.summary: Wisconsin native JJ Watt has been named lead analyst for the "NFL on CBS" in a new multiyear agreement.
articles.body:
NFL legend and Wisconsin native JJ Watt has officially been named lead analyst for the "NFL on CBS" in a new multiyear agreement. David Berson, chairman of Global Sports Group and Skydance, made the announcement in an Oct. 22 news release .

Watt joined CBS in 2023 as a studio analyst before moving into the booth to call games with Ian Eagle last season on CBS' No. 2 team.

This summer, Watt landed a promotion to replace another Wisconsin native, Tony Romo, on CBS Sports' lead NFL broadcasting team on an interim basis. That came when Romo, the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback, had been placed on leave soon after he was cited for OWI in Milwaukee in July.

In early October, the network said that "CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways." Romo had been CBS' lead analyst on NFL game broadcasts since 2017.

Watt will continue calling the network's top games alongside play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson as CBS Sports' lead NFL announce team, the Oct. 22 announcement said. That'll include next season when they call Super Bowl 52 in Atlanta.

Watt shared how he found out about the promotion and what it means to him in an Oct. 22 video on X .

On Monday morning, Oct. 19, he said he got his kids up and, after breakfast, noticed a missed call from Berson.

"I'm thinking to myself, 'Aw, man, missed call from the boss. Am I in trouble, for potentially breaking Jim Nantz's hand on the broadcast on Sunday with our ball drill?" Watt said.

Turns out it was "significantly better news."

"He told me on that call that I would be the lead analyst for CBS moving forward," Watt said in the video. "Super Bowl next year and all that comes with that."

Watt thanked Berson and everybody involved for putting their trust in him.

"It is a true honor and a privilege and I do not take that responsibility lightly at all," he said. "I appreciate their trust in me. And I have an absolute blast doing it every single week, and I cannot wait to continue to do it."

Watt, a former Wisconsin Badgers All-American, retired from the NFL in 2022 after 12 seasons in a career that included winning the NFL Defensive Player of the Year award three times.

articles.title: Packers HC Matt LaFleur Facing Potential Punishment From NFL
articles.summary: It’s mostly positive vibes for the Green Bay Packers right now.They have won three games in a row, and are getting star running back Josh Jacobs back. Green...
articles.body:
It's mostly positive vibes for the Green Bay Packers right now.

They have won three games in a row, and are getting star running back Josh Jacobs back. Green Bay is preparing to take on the Detroit Lions on Sunday, but something could come back to bite coach Matt LaFleur from last week's matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Green Bay Packers HC Matt LaFleur Could Get Fined for Publicly Criticizing Officials

The Packers' defense was penalized for roughing the passer three times during their win over the Cowboys. After the game, coach Matt LaFleur voiced his displeasure with the inconsistencies of when roughing the passer gets called, especially considering quarterback Jordan Love has yet to receive one in his favor.

"I think just in regards to all that stuff, at the end of the day, you just want it to be called both ways," LaFleur said. "So, if they're going to call it one way, it should be called for the other team, as well, and I feel like there's been a lot of times when Jordan's taken some close to potential roughing calls, and he's not getting the calls."

Matt LaFleur May Be Willing to Fall on the Sword for His Team

The analysts on The Green Bay Beat discussed how it may be worth it for LaFleur to eat a fine if it gets the officials to call roughing the passer on a more even basis.

"It's 6-0 on roughing the passer penalties this year," Bill Huber said.

"It's the consistency of it versus the big, emotional interaction," Paul Bretl said. "It's talking about it pregame. Its's being in the refs ear every single time. Like hey, you called that on us but not on them, and vice versa. Just the consistency of it, so it's always front of mind for the referee."

"I don't know how much more he's accomplishing by venting his frustrations publicly, on top of the clips they send to the league," Matt Schneidman said. "It could just put more public pressure on refs to maybe make some more calls. Maybe that's the way to go. If that doesn't change, LaFleur might need to take another step. He just got extended, you got plenty of money. It's for the better of the team."

As Schneidman mentioned, the Packers send clips to the league office each week to question or gain clarity on penalties that were or were not called. LaFleur said they also use those clips to teach their players what the NFL is looking for in certain penalties.

"We'll see what they say," LaFleur said. "I obviously can't tell you guys about what they say, but it helps us educate our players and at the end of the day that's our job. We got to educate them on what they can and cannot do and make sure that we try to coach them up and they got to control themselves in the moment."

articles.title: Mark Sanchez's change-of-plea hearing is canceled
articles.summary: In September, former NFL quarterback and former Fox broadcaster Mark Sanchez agreed to resolve multiple pending criminal charges with a guilty plea.
articles.body:
In September, former NFL quarterback and former Fox broadcaster Mark Sanchez agreed to resolve multiple pending criminal charges with a guilty plea. Since then, nothing else has happened as to the criminal case.

Via Fox 59, Sanchez's change-of-plea hearing was canceled . It had been set for November 9, after being rescheduled four times.

Per the report, the official docketing system doesn't explain the move. The entry says only that, "by agreement of the parties, change of plea hearing was vacated at this time."

When the plea deal was reached, Sanchez's lawyers requested a sentencing hearing on November 9 or November 16.

It could be as simple as the change-of-plea process being handled on paper, without a hearing. Still, there will need to be a sentencing hearing, at some point.

It's also possible that the plea deal has fallen apart. Now that Sanchez has settled Perry Tole's civil, the victim could be less motivated to tell the kind of compelling story that could lead to a conviction. Sanchez could be emboldened to rescind his agreement and fight.

Whatever the reason, it's strange. Reaching a deal is the hard part. Reducing it to writing and finalizing it is the easy part.

In the legal system, nothing is done until it's done. And Sanchez's criminal case currently shows no signs of being done, or of a foreseeable moment in court when it will get done.

articles.summary: Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans reacts to quarterback C.J. Stroud being named the AFC Offensive Player of the Week for Week 6.
articles.body:
After throwing for 312 passing yards and three touchdowns in the Houston Texans' Week 6 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, quarterback C.J. Stroud was named the AFC Offensive Player of the Year.

It was Stroud's first time being Offensive Player of the Week since Week 5 of last season. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans was happy to see the rest of the NFL finally acknowledge how Stroud has been performing all season.

"It's rewarding in the sense of everyone seeing it across the NFL, of what he's been doing, not just us, me talking about it all the time, of how well he's been having an offseason, Training Camp and all the way now to the start of the season," Ryans said. "It's been that way. He's been doing a great job since he's been back and he's done a great job leading us in the games as well. I'm happy that he's able to get that national recognition that he truly deserves."

Despite the Texans starting the year 0-4, Stroud has played well all year long. He has the scond-most passing yards and has only thrown on interception all season. Stroud's performance has finally paid off with wins each of the past two weeks against the Tennessee Titans and Jacksonville Jaguars.

Now, Houston is looking for their first win at home against the New York Giants who are first in the NFC East right now. With the Jaguars on bye, the Texans have a chance to be one win behind Jacksonville in the AFC South race. If they were to make the playoffs this season, it would be the second time in NFL history a team started 0-4 and made it to the postseason.

"You talk about a guy who's been consistent all year, leading the NFL in yards, leading this team to where we need to be at," Texans defensive end Will Anderson Jr. said. "He's playing outstanding. But it starts with his preparation. It starts with his process. You see him every day go through that same process, that same preparation, every day on the field. It's no shocker that when we get in the game, he's making big plays. He's commanding the offense and he's taking over and winning these games for us."

articles.title: Allen Bailey cause of death: Former Chiefs star, 9-year NFL vet dead at 37
articles.summary: Former Kansas City Chiefs defensive end Allen Bailey has passed away at 37, according to multiple ex-teammates.
articles.body:
On Tuesday night, tributes began pouring out for former Kansas City Chiefs defensive lineman Allen Bailey. Former NFL and college teammates were paying their respects to Bailey, who has reportedly passed away.

Bailey was just 37 years old. At the time of this posting, no cause of death has been confirmed, but several people close to him have acknowledged his death.

Among the first to honor Bailey was Colin McCarthy, his former college football teammate with the Miami Hurricanes. " Lost a fellow brother today ," McCarthy wrote on X. "Prayers to AB family! Love you Big Cuzzo!"

Jeff Allen, who was selected by the Chiefs in the second round of the 2012 NFL Draft, also paid his respects. Allen, who spent two years in Kansas City, wrote: "Lost a teammate, a friend, a brother. God needed another angel . Rest easy, my brother."

Bailey grew up on Sapelo Island, Georgia, which you can only access by ferry reservations, or a pre-registered tour approved by state officials, the Georgia Department of Natural Resources, or an island resident. The listed population is just 70 residents, though Bailey has said the real number is in the 50s.

Despite the small, secluded community Bailey grew up in, he blossomed into an incredible talent. He didn't play organized football until seventh grade, but eventually was recruited by the University of Miami and went on to star for the Hurricanes.

Bailey earned first-team All-ACC honors before going on to have a 10-year NFL career.

Our deepest condolences go out to Bailey's family and friends during this incredibly difficult and tragic time.

articles.title: Is Saquon Barkley back from injury vs Cowboys? Latest from Eagles coach
articles.summary: Is Saquon Barkley back from injury heading into the Eagles next game vs Cowboys?
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA − The Eagles could have running back Saquon Barkley at practice this week after he missed most of four games this season with various injuries, including the last two games with a hamstring injury.

Barkley suffered the injury in the first quarter against the Los Angeles Rams on Oct. 4. He sat out the rest of that game, then the next two games against Jacksonville and Carolina. The Eagles face the Dallas Cowboys on Oct. 26.

Eagles coach Nick Sirianni wouldn't say if Barkley will be available against the Cowboys, but he did make it seem like Barkley will participate as the Eagles begin their practice week on Oct. 22.

"Saquon's a phenomenal football player, phenomenal leader, captain," Sirianni said. "So anytime you have an opportunity to get someone like him back out on the field, that's huge. We'll see where we are as the week progresses. "Looking forward to seeing him out there (Oct. 22). "We'll see where we are at the end of it."

Barkley also left the game against the Tennessee Titans on Sept. 20 after the first offensive play because of a stinger. Barkley returned in the third quarter, then left for good in the fourth.

For the season, Barkley has 182 yards rushing while averaging 5.1 yards per carry. In the two full games that Barkley played in, he had 83 yards in the season-opener against the Commanders on Sept. 13 (5.5 yards per carry), and 82 yards against the Bears on Sept. 28 (also 5.5 yards per carry).

Eagles vs. Panthers. 9 key plays that led to Philadelphia's loss

Sirianni said Barkley's return will boost the Eagles' running game, which ranks 29th in the NFL. The Eagles have especially struggled when quarterbacks Jalen Hurts and Tanner McKee have lined up under center and tried play-action passes.

The opposing defenses, not respecting the running game, have often blitzed in those situations.

"Your play-action pass game gets better and better as you run the football better, right?" Sirianni said. "And so, we have to play not only complementary football on offense, defense, and special teams, but also within the offense. For your play-action game to create the plays that you want it to create, your run game's got to be going.

"But anytime you add a player of Saquon's caliber to your team, that's obviously a huge plus."

As for other injured players, it's not known yet if edge rushers Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle), Nolan Smith (concussion) or Jonathan Greenard (ankle) can practice. And left guard Landon Dickerson (knee) is beginning his second week of the 21-day practice window as he works to return from injured reserve.

In addition C Drew Kendall (knee) is expected to continue practicing this week after missing the previous two games with a knee injury. Kendall was on the game-day roster against the Panthers, but would have only played in an emergency situation as Jake Majors started for the second straight game.

Nick Sirianni fined $250,000 for behavior towards referees

Sirianni was fined $250,000 for conduct toward NFL game officials, according to a report from Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer .

Sirianni was reportedly one of three head coaches fined $250K for their conduct. The others are Patriots coach Mike Vrabel and Jets coach Aaron Glenn. According to Breer's report, the fines are reportedly on hold and "could be repealed with good behavior."

Sirianni has had run-ins with referees and fans over the years, and is known for being fiery on the sidelines at times. It's not known if a specific incident occurred this season to incur the fine.

"I won't get into my conversations with the league," Sirianni said when asked about the fine. "I truly believe that I've been in constant growth of maturity of in every phase."

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Latest on QB's Status for Ravens vs. Bengals After Practice Return
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson could be a full participant in practice for the first time since injuring his ankle in Week 4.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson could be a full participant in practice for the first time since injuring his ankle in Week 4.

The Ravens shared a video of Jackson jogging out in uniform for the start of Thursday's practice after returning Wednesday in a limited capacity.

Jackson has been sidelined for two games since suffering a left ankle sprain Oct. 4.

The Ravens are preparing for a Sunday matchup against the visiting Cincinnati Bengals.
